root_cause.text: In the `isert_login_recv_done()` function of the IB/isert subsystem, the login request payload length is calculated by subtracting `ISER_HEADERS_LEN` from `wc->byte_len` without validating that `wc->byte_len` is at least `ISER_HEADERS_LEN`, causing an integer underflow when processing short PDUs.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description states the computation occurs "with no lower bound," allowing underflow if `wc->byte_len` is fewer than 76 bytes, and the patch introduces a check `if (unlikely(wc->byte_len < ISER_HEADERS_LEN))` prior to the subtraction to enforce this constraint.

intent_record.how: Prevents integer underflow and invalid memory operations by returning early when the received login packet is shorter than the required header size.

candidates.rationale: This statement calculates the login request payload length by subtracting ISER_HEADERS_LEN from wc->byte_len. It lacks validation to ensure wc->byte_len is at least ISER_HEADERS_LEN, causing an unsigned integer underflow when processing short PDUs where wc->byte_len < ISER_HEADERS_LEN.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement calculates the login request payload length by subtracting ISER_HEADERS_LEN from wc->byte_len without any validation. When wc->byte_len is less than ISER_HEADERS_LEN (processing short PDUs), this causes an unsigned integer underflow because byte_len wraps around to a very large value. The fix intent was to add validation to prevent this arithmetic underflow and ensure only complete login headers are processed.
